```{r}

# Assignment 1 - Data Analysis using R Programming

# Import dataset
healthcare_dataset <- read.csv("healthcare_dataset.csv")

# View first few rows
head(healthcare_dataset)

# 1. Print structure of Dataset
str(healthcare_dataset)

# 2. List of variables in Dataset
names(healthcare_dataset)

# 3. Print top 15 rows of Dataset
head(healthcare_dataset, 15)

# 4. User-defined function using a variable from the dataset
age_group <- function(age) 
  {
  if (age >= 65) {
    return("Senior")
  } else {
    return("Adult")
  }
}
# Test the function
age_group(70)

# 5. Filter rows
library(dplyr)

senior_patients <- healthcare_dataset %>% filter(Age >= 65)

head(senior_patients)

# 6. Dependent and independent variables

# Independent variable
age_data <- healthcare_dataset["Age"]

# Dependent variable
billing_data <- healthcare_dataset["Billing.Amount"]

# Combine both variables
healthcare_analysis <- cbind(age_data, billing_data)
# Display the new data frame
head(healthcare_analysis)

# 7. Check for missing values
sum(is.na(healthcare_dataset))
# No missing values were found, so no rows were removed

# 8. Check for duplicated rows
sum(duplicated(healthcare_dataset))

# 8A  Extra step -Remove duplicated rows
healthcare_clean <- healthcare_dataset %>% distinct()
nrow(healthcare_clean)

# 9. Reorder rows by Billing Amount in descending order
healthcare_sorted <- healthcare_clean %>% arrange(desc(Billing.Amount))
head(healthcare_sorted, 10)

# 10. Rename columns
healthcare_renamed <- healthcare_clean %>% rename(
Billing_Amount = Billing.Amount,
Medical_Condition = Medical.Condition
)
names(healthcare_renamed)

# 11. Create a new variable using a mathematical function
healthcare_new <- healthcare_renamed %>% mutate(Billing_Double = Billing_Amount * 2)
head(healthcare_new)

# 12. Create a training set using random sampling

set.seed(123)

training_data <- healthcare_new %>% sample_frac(0.80)
nrow(training_data)

# 13. Summary statistics
summary(healthcare_new)

# 14. Mean of Age
mean(healthcare_new$Age)

# 15. Median of Age
median(healthcare_new$Age)

# 16. Mode of Age
get_mode <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

get_mode(healthcare_new$Age)

# 17. Range of Age
range(healthcare_new$Age)

# 18. Scatter plot
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(healthcare_new, aes(x = Age, y = Billing_Amount)) + geom_point(color= "blue")

# 19. Bar plot (1 variable)
ggplot(healthcare_new, aes(x = Medical_Condition)) + geom_bar(fill = "steelblue")

# 19A. Bar plot using two variables
ggplot(healthcare_new, aes(x = Medical_Condition, fill = Admission.Type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")

# 20. Pearson correlation
cor(healthcare_new$Age, healthcare_new$Billing_Amount, method = "pearson")

```
